items.text: SEASON 6 · EPISODE 3 · DRAFT · CASE-031  Design studio and courthouse · Maya, Priya, Ruth and Judge Obi · Level L4 · Intermediate support  The courthouse is over budget. Item 14 on the contractor’s cost list deletes court recorder B — “a duplicate.”  ⚑ RV-144: the record’s requirements are the court’s. RV-141: figures illustrative. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: Value-Engineered
items.stakes: A cost list deletes the courthouse's second recorder as ‘a duplicate’. The workshop is Friday; the court's record is on the line.
items.reward: Two independent copies of the record. An informed owner. Ruth still speaking to you.

objectives.text: Find out what B really is
Change how VE lists are answered
Look closer: two things about the record

items.rumor: The cheapest thing on the list was the only thing that couldn't fail with the rest.

items.alt: Ruth, the contractor's project manager, in a hi-vis vest and holding a cost report, at Linden Row's long table. Priya listens.

bubbles.text: VE-14: delete court recorder B. It's a duplicate. Eighteen thousand four hundred back to the county.
Maya, can we sign that off by Friday?

items.caption: The workshop is Friday. The owner wants a number.

lines.text: Eighteen thousand four hundred. It's a duplicate. Everyone duplicates recorders and nobody ever uses the second one.
Nobody uses a seatbelt either, until the day.

items.prompt: 2:15 p.m. How do you answer VE-14?
items.risk: A courtroom whose record can be lost.

hints.text: Whose rule decides how many copies the record needs?

options.label: Sign it off — it says duplicate
options.result: The county banks 18,400. Nobody asks the court.
options.consequence: A function deleted without anyone naming it.
options.fail: A cut signed without its function.

options.label: Write what B does and what depends on it, check the court's standard, and bring numbers
options.result: The court's standard §4 requires a second, independent copy.

options.label: Reject the whole VE list
options.result: Ruth: “Then the county cuts the second courtroom instead.”
options.consequence: A no without numbers loses the argument.

options.label: Keep B on the drawings and ignore VE-14
options.result: Priya: “The owner decides value engineering. We inform it.”
options.consequence: Hiding from the owner's decision isn't design.
options.fail: Value engineering is the owner's decision.

items.title: Not a duplicate.
items.body: The court's recording standard, §4: *the official record shall be kept in two copies that do not share a point of failure.* Recorder B is the second copy. VE-14 was never sent to the court.
items.label: Test: what is B — and whose decision is it?

items.sub: Intermediate · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Priya and Maya beside a board. Availability: MTBF over MTBF plus MTTR. Two recorders that fail independently: one minus the chance both are down. Eight thousand hours between failures, forty-eight to repair… point nine nine four. The pair: point nine nine nine nine six. If they fail independently. Find out what they share.

items.text: 📗 FIELD NOTES · INTERMEDIATE  Terms   Availability   MTBF   MTTR   Value engineering   Formula and variables   ƒ FORMULA · Availability — one unit and a redundant pair  A = MTBF ÷ (MTBF + MTTR) · A pair  = 1 − (1 − A) 2    MTBF  mean time between failures, hours  MTTR  mean time to repair, hours  A  fraction of time a unit works  A pair   fraction of time at least one of two works     ƒ FORMULA · Percentage  % = part ÷ whole × 100   part  the piece you are measuring  whole  everything it is part of

items.alt: In the courthouse, an empty courtroom under renovation. Judge Obi, in a dark suit and glasses, listens to Maya.

bubbles.text: VE-14 would replace recorder B with a copy of A's file.
A copy of a thing that has failed is also a thing that has failed.

items.prompt: Look, I'm not trying to break the courthouse. I'm trying to land a budget. Tell me what I'm really cutting.

options.label: “Here's what B does, what depends on it, and the hours a year it saves. The court decides whether it can go.”
options.reply: That I can take to the owner. Thank you for not just saying no.

options.label: “You're cutting the court's record. No.”
options.reply: Then give me something I can put in front of the owner.

options.label: “Can we find the saving somewhere else?”
options.reply: Maybe. Show me what B's worth first.

items.title: Separate power.
items.body: Tracing it through: recorder A, the mixer and the proposed ‘copy 2’ all sit on UPS 1 in the courtroom. B is on UPS 2 in the IT room, with its own mic inputs. In the old courthouse, B was still recording the afternoon UPS 1 died mid-sentencing.
items.label: Test: what survives a UPS 1 failure — and what does the pair formula assume?

items.title: The Apollo 13 lesson
items.body: In April 1970, an oxygen tank explosion crippled the Apollo 13 service module. The crew survived partly because the lunar module had independent power, oxygen and propulsion — systems designed for a different job that shared almost nothing with the failed one. Engineers still quote it: redundancy that shares a failure isn't redundancy.

items.alt: Two boxes: UPS 1 in the courtroom carrying the mixer, recorder A and the proposed copy; UPS 2 in the IT room carrying recorder B, marked deleted by VE-14.
items.caption: The ‘saving’ puts both copies on one UPS.

items.title: §4 · two independent copies
items.body: Section 4 of the court's recording standard: *the official record shall be kept in two copies that do not share a point of failure.* The VE list had never been sent to the court.

items.label: **Fix it:** give the record a second copy that can't fail with the first.

items.prompt: Thursday afternoon. The court wants two independent copies. How does B survive?
known: ◉ ≈ 52 h/yr down with one recorder; ≈ 0.3 h with two
items.risk: A record that fails with its only backup.
timeout: Friday's workshop starts without your statement.

hints.text: What would make copy 2 share nothing with copy 1?

options.label: Keep B on UPS 2 with its own passive mic split; send the court and owner the function statement and the numbers
options.result: The court puts it in writing; the owner rejects VE-14 and takes the saving from the lobby display upgrade.

options.label: Keep B, but move it next to A on UPS 1 to save a circuit
Accept the file copy — it's cheaper
options.result: The first UPS 1 fault costs a day of testimony and a retrial motion.
options.fail: A copy of a failure is a failure.

options.label: Tell Ruth it's a legal requirement and walk out
options.result: Ruth has no letter, no numbers, nothing to show the owner.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #54 · AVERY'S LENS  Say what it does before you say what it costs  Every line in a design exists for a function; a cut that doesn't name the function it removes isn't a saving, it's a risk moved to someone else.  VE-14 called recorder B ‘a duplicate’. It was the only thing keeping the court's record alive when recorder A's power failed.

items.alt: The same two boxes after the fix: UPS 2 carries recorder B with its own mic split, the independent copy 2.
items.caption: Two copies. Two UPSs. Two sets of inputs.

items.prompt: Friday, after the workshop. How should the studio answer VE lists from now on?

hints.text: What should every cut arrive with?

options.label: Every VE item goes back with a function statement — what it does, what depends on it, the numbers, and who decides — before anyone signs
options.result: Ruth starts sending VE lists with a ‘function’ column already filled in.

options.label: Refuse all VE on principle
options.result: The next project picks another consultant.

options.label: Priya answers them all personally
options.result: Priya answers them all personally, badly, at midnight.

options.label: Nothing — VE-14 is rejected
options.result: VE-22 deletes the backup encoder at the Playhouse next month.

items.title: UPS 2 · IT room
items.body: Recorder B's UPS isn't in the courtroom at all. It's in the IT room two floors down — which is why, in the old courthouse, B was still recording the afternoon the courtroom UPS died during a sentencing hearing.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  A = MTBF ÷ (MTBF + MTTR); a pair is 1 − (1 − A)² only if nothing is shared — power, inputs, network, software. Answer every value-engineering item with its function, its dependencies and its numbers, and let the owner and the court decide.
REFLECTION (optional)  · Ruth wasn’t the villain; she had a budget to land. How do you argue with someone whose problem is real?
